refactoring-oop-services.label: Refactoring OOP Services
refactoring-oop-services.summary: Refactor working OOP code by moving list-wide coordination into focused services while keeping object-specific behavior on the model and main.py thin.

sketch1.title: Keep model and service responsibilities separate

try_refactoring_oop_services_sketch0.title: Extract a working report loop into ReportService
try_refactoring_oop_services_sketch0.prompt: `main.py` already works, and `models/book.py` already owns `Book.display_line()`. Refactor the list-wide report logic into `ReportService.build_report(self, books)` in `services/report_service.py`. The service must build the report from each Book's existing `display_line()` result and return the single newline-separated string. Then update `main.py` to import `ReportService`, remove the old report-building `for` loop, and print the value returned by `build_report(books)`. Preserve the same visible output.
try_refactoring_oop_services_sketch0.hint: Move the collection coordination, not the one-book formatting. `Book.display_line()` already owns that behavior.

help.concept: A safe refactor moves list-wide work into the service while the model keeps its per-object behavior and the output stays stable.
help.hint_1: The service can collect each `book.display_line()` result.
help.hint_2: After the move, main.py should call the service instead of keeping the report loop.

try_refactoring_oop_services_sketch0.starterCode:
from models.book import Book

first_title = input()
first_price = int(input())
second_title = input()
second_price = int(input())

books = [
    Book(first_title, first_price),
    Book(second_title, second_price),
]

lines = []
for book in books:
    lines.append(book.display_line())

print("\n".join(lines))

1.message: Remove the old collection loop from main.py and print the report returned by `ReportService.build_report(books)`.

2.message: `build_report(self, books)` should coordinate the collection using each Book's existing `display_line()` behavior.

try_refactoring_oop_services_sketch1.title: Move collection filtering into CatalogService
try_refactoring_oop_services_sketch1.prompt: `main.py` already works, and `Book.is_affordable(max_price)` already owns the one-book affordability rule. Refactor the list-wide filtering into `CatalogService.affordable_titles(self, books, max_price)` in `services/catalog_service.py`. The service must use each Book's existing `is_affordable(max_price)` method and return the matching titles in input order. Then update `main.py` to import and call `CatalogService`, remove the old filtering `for` loop, and keep printing the returned titles joined with ` | `. Preserve the same visible behavior.
try_refactoring_oop_services_sketch1.hint: The model decides whether one book is affordable; the service decides which titles to collect from the whole list.

help.concept: A focused service coordinates a collection without stealing the object-specific rule from the model.
help.hint_2: main.py should only create books, call the service, and display the returned titles.

try_refactoring_oop_services_sketch1.starterCode:
from models.book import Book

max_price = int(input())

books = [
    Book(input(), int(input())),
    Book(input(), int(input())),
    Book(input(), int(input())),
]

titles = []
for book in books:
    if book.is_affordable(max_price):
        titles.append(book.title)

print(" | ".join(titles))

mc-refactor-benefits.title: Recognize a successful refactor
mc-refactor-benefits.prompt: Which TWO outcomes show that moving report logic from `main.py` into a service was a useful refactor?
mc-refactor-benefits.hint: The responsibility should move while observable behavior stays stable.

help.concept: Refactoring changes structure without changing the program's promised behavior.
help.hint_1: The old output should still be produced.
help.hint_2: The collection-wide responsibility should have one clear home.

options.a: main.py becomes thinner because the collection-wide report logic lives in a service
options.b: The refactor changes the report format at the same time
options.c: The same input still produces the same visible report
options.d: The old loop remains duplicated in main.py and the service

mc-safe-refactor-steps.title: Choose safe refactoring steps
mc-safe-refactor-steps.prompt: Which THREE actions make an OOP service refactor safer?
mc-safe-refactor-steps.hint: Move one responsibility, reconnect the caller, and verify behavior.

help.concept: Small structural moves are safer when imports/calls are updated and behavior is checked after the move.
help.hint_1: Do not mix unrelated behavior changes into the same refactor.
help.hint_2: Keep a way to compare before and after behavior.

options.a: Move one collection-wide responsibility at a time
options.b: Update the caller to import and use the new service
options.c: Change output rules during the same refactor
options.d: Run the program or tests again after the move

sc-main-role.title: Keep main.py thin
sc-main-role.prompt: After list-wide filtering and reporting move into services, what should `main.py` mainly do?
sc-main-role.hint: Think about wiring pieces together rather than owning their internal logic.

help.concept: The entry script should mainly create objects, call services, and display returned results.
help.hint_1: Models and services should own the reusable behavior.
help.hint_2: main.py is the coordinator at the application boundary.

options.a: Create objects, call service methods, and display returned results
options.b: Keep duplicate copies of every service loop as a backup
options.c: Move one-book methods out of the model and into print statements
options.d: Avoid imports by keeping every responsibility in main.py
